subject: Latency spike after model roll — request to activate traffic fencing
messages:
From: Alex Pelton <alex.pelton@clearsky.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 jump after v12q rollout

Diego,

We pushed traffic to your v12q model this morning (09:00 PT) following the canary. Since ~09:10 our p95 has increased by ~450ms on production routes, and a small subset of calls are timing out. Our SRE team collected logs and a timeline snapshot (attached).

Quick summary:
- Impact: p95 from 220ms -> ~670ms across our high-throughput endpoints
- First seen: 09:10 PT, sustained for ~35 minutes, then intermittent
- Notable: error rate stayed low (~0.2%) but tail latency exploded on long-context flows

We need an urgent ask: can Redwood activate a traffic-fencing policy or pin our traffic to the previous model variant while you investigate? Our SLA obligations require us to keep p95 under 300ms for these routes and customers are already calling the desk.

Happy to hop on a bridge — ops@clearsky.ai is on standby.

Thanks,
Alex Pelton
VP Engineering | ClearSky Analytics
Phone: +1 415 555 0192

Attachments: p95-sample-logs.zip (log bundle), timeline-snapshot.csv (route-level metrics)
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Pelton <alex.pelton@clearsky.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 16:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump after v12q rollout

Alex — thanks for the rapid heads-up and for the artifacts. I reviewed the logs and the spike aligns with the v12q rollout window.

Immediate plan (proposed):
1) Enable a temporary traffic-fence for ClearSky routes to pin to v11y (previous variant) — this is a non-disruptive routing change and should restore p95 within minutes.
2) Open a rollback ticket to retract v12q from production until we finish causal analysis.
3) Run a focused diagnostic (KV cache behavior, sequence-length-specific kernel path) against the failing traces.

I need approval for the traffic-fence activation and a quick confirmation you accept a short SLA carveout while we perform the rollback/diagnostics (we'll document the window). If you approve, I will execute step 1 and notify you when traffic is fenced.

If helpful, we can stand up a joint bridge now — ping me and I’ll pull in infra.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Technical Account Manager | Redwood Inference

On Sat, Jun 20, 2026 at 09:12 -0700 Alex Pelton <alex.pelton@clearsky.ai> wrote:

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 17:00:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Sudden p95 jump after v12q rollout — ops steps and approval request

Diego / Kimberly —

I dug into the canary telemetry and correlated infra logs. Quick notes:
- The regressions are concentrated on long-context routes (>1k tokens) where the new attention optimization in v12q takes a different kernel path.
- Memory/CPU on hosts look stable; the degradation looks algorithmic rather than resource saturation.
- We have a clear rollback to v11y ready to deploy (variant pin + routing change) and can enact a traffic fence that pins ClearSky's routing to v11y for the next 3 hours.

Operational impact of a traffic-fence:
- Will roll back ClearSky traffic only (no global rollback).
- Expected p95 improvement in 3–7 minutes after change.
- We'll log the change as a provisional SLA carveout window and surface to Finance if needed.

Approvals needed from leadership:
1) Kimberly — approval to activate the traffic-fence now and sign the temporary SLA tolerance (we will timebox to 3 hours).
2) Diego — confirm ClearSky consents to the carveout (Alex, please reply-all to approve)

If we get thumbs-up I’ll schedule the change and post the runbook link (will include rollback steps).

Ben Carter
Director, Reliability | Redwood Inference

Attachments: (none)
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Alex Pelton <alex.pelton@clearsky.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 02:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump after v12q rollout — ops steps and approval request

All —

Approved.

Conditions and notes:
- Traffic-fence activation authorized for ClearSky Analytics only, effective immediately upon this message.
- Timebox: 3 hours from activation. If diagnostics require more time, Diego/Ben must escalate to me with explicit justification.
- SLA carveout: Redwood authorizes a provisional tolerance for p95 during the 3-hour window; we will document start/end times and any customer notices. Finance/Legal notified separately.
- Required artifacts before we re-open traffic to v12q: causal RCA (ops + runtime), reproducer run, and a postmortem with regression test added to the onboarding checklist.

Diego — please run the traffic-fence and confirm when the routing change completes. Alex — we appreciate the log bundle; please send any extra traces that hit the long-context path if you have them.

Authorization code: KF-2026-06-21-0615 (internal reference).

Kimberly Park
VP Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
